verdicts.line: The dirt paths you walked are paver stone now. The huddles you met have settled and built. A generation has passed, and the world has moved on its own.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: A freshly walked trail renders as compacted earth — the ground remembering you — and becomes paver stone after one generation passes.
verdicts.reason: Captures the per-tile aging mechanic (dirt→stone after one generation) and the specific 'ground remembering you' phrasing from the visual canon.

verdicts.line: Where people stopped wandering, they built. Roads have hardened into stone. The settlements that rooted here carry what you did, and what the world did without you.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Where tribes crossed the threshold of feeling, they stopped moving and raised walls.
verdicts.reason: Loses the asymmetric settlement identity (Hope settlements vs Fear walled camps) that is core to uhta's pole mechanics.
verdicts.correction: Roads have hardened into stone. Where tribes crossed the threshold of feeling, they stopped wandering — Hope rooted into settlements, Fear dug into walled camps.

verdicts.line: The ground remembers everywhere you walked — stone roads now, carrying travelers in your color. Where tribes crossed the threshold of feeling, they stopped moving and raised walls.

verdicts.reason: Preserves both the 'ground remembering' phrase and the allegiance-colored roads carrying same-pole travelers from the road-following mechanic.

verdicts.line: Trails have become stone. The nomads you met have children now, and some have built where they stopped believing motion mattered more than what they felt.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: A freshly walked trail renders as compacted earth — the ground remembering you — and becomes paver stone after one generation passes.
verdicts.reason: The 'stopped believing motion mattered more than what they felt' is a concrete restatement of the settling threshold (devotion → permanence) without abstraction.

verdicts.line: The paths are stone. The wanderers have settled. What was temporary when you last woke has rooted — villages stand where devotion held, and the roads you walked carry the next generation.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Each tribe adds ~2 regular NPCs per sleep (after the world forms; genesis suppresses births during formation, and schism's pop-cap bounds it thereafter). Newborns start at 0 — apathy.
verdicts.reason: The phrase 'have children now' invokes the newborn mechanic but loses the critical detail that newborns are born grey/apathetic, not inheriting belief.
verdicts.correction: The paths are stone. The wanderers have settled. What was temporary when you last woke has rooted — villages stand where devotion held, and the roads you walked carry the next generation born grey into a colored world.

verdicts.line: Stone roads connect what were dirt paths. Tribes that reached conviction have built and stopped wandering. The landscape answers what happened while you slept — settlements, walls, and the hardened ground you made by walking.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: A tribe whose average enters the devout band (|value| ≥ 6) and holds it for a generation stops wandering and settles as what it feels — Hope roots into an open settlement, Fear digs into a walled camp.
verdicts.reason: Captures the settling rule (conviction → building) and the asymmetric architecture (settlements vs walls) without numbers.

verdicts.line: Your footprints are stone roads now. Tribes have stopped drifting and raised what they believe — walled camps, settlements, the bones of permanence. The world has aged a generation since you last opened your eyes.
verdicts.quoted_chunk: Your footprints are stone roads now.
verdicts.reason: The 'footprints are stone roads' is a concrete physical translation of the per-tile aging mechanic, and 'raised what they believe' captures the settling-as-what-it-feels rule.
